raw_response:
*(speaking in my own voice, thinking out loud)*

Aiya, another year. My back's not what it was but the land don't farm itself. Two of my boys are off in town at the factory now so it's just me and the wife mostly, plus the grandkids when school lets out. Seven mouths but only two of us really in the fields every day.

Eight and a half mu — same land I been working since before Reform. I know every patch of it. The soil on the west side is better, holds water, so that's where I put the wheat-corn. The east side is sandier, dries out faster, so cotton goes there. Always been that way.

**My wheat** — already in the ground since October, it's greening up now. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer for every three mu back at planting, that's what I always do. Now's the time for top-dress. I'll put down one bag of urea per two mu when I irrigate at jointing — one bag of urea, one watering, together, saves me a trip. If the wheat looks yellow I might put a little extra but it looks OK this year. Wife and me will walk it. Harvest by combine like everyone, I pay the combine man 50 yuan per mu, done in an afternoon.

**My corn** — goes in right after the wheat comes off in June. Very tight, maybe five days between. No time to plow properly, I just use the no-till planter the cooperative rents out, put the seed right through the wheat stubble. Hybrid seed from the agro shop, the one my nephew used last year did alright so I'll try that again. Bag of compound goes down with the planter, then a bag of urea top-dress when it's knee-high. Watch the weather — if July is dry I'll water once, but pumping costs money so I try to let the sky do it.

**My cotton** — this is the one takes all my time. Three mu on the east side. Planting it now actually, mid-April. I buy certified seed, can't save cotton seed anymore like the old days. Bag of compound per mu at planting. The bollworms been bad the last few years so I'll spray maybe three-four times through the summer — can't skip it or they eat everything. Picking in the fall, me and the wife pick what we can, the girls come help on weekends. If there's too much I'll get a neighbor to help for a few days for wages.

**Money** — I got maybe 5,000 yuan from what the boys sent home and what I saved. That covers seed and fertilizer if I'm careful. I don't buy the fancy foreign fertilizer, just the regular compound. If prices jump I cut back on top-dress, not on base — base is what sets the crop.

I don't change much year to year. What works works. Last year I got about 400 jin of wheat per mu (that's 400 kg, decent year, had enough rain), corn was maybe 450, cotton was not great, maybe 220 jin lint per mu. About the same this year if Heaven cooperates.
